_comment: The onlooker.dev zone's ONE rate limiting rule. This file is canonical:
apps/api/DEPLOYMENT.md explains the reasoning and points here for the
expression, rather than restating it. Apply with scripts/cloudflare/apply.sh.
ONE RULE IS THE WHOLE BUDGET. The plan allows a single rate limiting rule,
so this is not a rule among several that can be narrowed freely - it is all
the rate limiting the API has, at the edge or anywhere else. Removing a path
from the expression removes the only limit that path has.
WHY THESE PATHS. Each one takes no credential and costs something real.
/auth/forgot-password reaches sendEmail unauthenticated, so without a
limit anyone can mail-bomb a known address and burn the Resend quota.
This is the expensive one.
/auth/login verifies a password - CPU, and the credential-stuffing
surface. The per-account backoff in db/login-attempts.ts keys on the
submitted address, so it does not slow one IP spraying many addresses;
that is the case this per-IP limit covers.
/auth/signup creates an account. It sends no mail; the mail cap in
apps/api/src/db/mail-sends.ts covers the three routes that do.
/auth/reset-password takes a token worth guessing at volume.
/api/orgs/invites/verify runs a SHA-256 and an indexed D1 read with no
credential. Token brute force is not the concern - 32 bytes of crypto
random - unmetered D1 reads are, the same concern as the lessons path.
/api/public/lessons/ runs a D1 read per request and nothing caches it,
not the hit and not the miss.
WHY /auth/refresh IS EXCLUDED, despite also being unauthenticated: every
active browser session calls it periodically, so behind a corporate NAT or
a mobile carrier a shared per-IP counter would throttle real users. Guessing
a random refresh token is not a realistic attack; legitimate volume is.
/auth/logout, /auth/verify-email and /auth/reset-password/verify are cheap.
/auth/resend-verification sits behind a session.
THE LIMITS ARE THE ONES THE ZONE ALREADY HAD, deliberately unchanged when
the four /auth/* paths and the invite verify path were added on 2026-10-17.
Widening the expression is purely additive protection; rewriting the numbers
at the same time would have loosened the one limit that actually worked.
cf.colo.id in the characteristics means the counter is PER DATACENTER as
well as per IP, so the practical ceiling is a multiple of 6 per 10s. The
10-second mitigation_timeout is what makes this tolerable on /auth/login
behind a shared NAT: a tripped limit clears almost immediately.
HISTORY, because it is the reason this file exists. Until 2026-10-17 the
rule lived only in the dashboard and DEPLOYMENT.md described it from
memory - five paths at 60 requests per minute per IP. The zone held one
path at 6 per 10 seconds per IP per colo. Four unauthenticated endpoints
the document promised were metered were not. See ONL-171. A description of
a thing is not the thing; this file is the thing.
description: unauthenticated surfaces that cost something real
